observed_anchors.observation: At the pre-PR744 main baseline, OP_HOSTCALL globally required exact Python int values before invoking a host handler even though String constants already existed in the serialized VM.
The pre-PR744 legacy request bridge looked up a Python mapping key without repeating exact request-id typing at the host boundary.

Parallel candidate PR #744 already moves scalar hostcall typing into typed host handlers and explicitly checks type(request_id) is int in the legacy v0 process handler. This functionally covers the production fence developed independently in PR #746.

hypothesis: If non-Int scalar transport is admitted to ClayVM hostcalls, trusting Python mapping lookup for legacy Int request IDs can admit a semantically wrong value through equality aliasing unless the host boundary repeats exact type identity.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The VM-level type gate is sufficient and host handlers do not need an independent exact type fence.
discriminator: Admit request ID 1, retain the real Int control, then present Python boolean true directly to the host process handler. Python dictionaries treat True and 1 as equal keys, so a missing exact-type fence can select request 1.
